from.place: Proof paragraph 2 of prop-coef-integral-exceptional-adjoint, main-20261015 .proof.md: the coherent finite-level mapping-complex adjunction in the middle R lim comparison. Fixed-object strict dg free/forgetful graph adjunction used before passage to coherent coefficient diagrams.

title: Fixed-object dg model structure and derived free graph adjunction
statement:
Use the universe and infinity-category conventions of [def-coef-complete-algebroid] and the projective model of unbounded cochain complexes $\mathbf V=\operatorname{Ch}(\mathbf Z)$ of [lem-coef-projective-chains-monoidal-model]. Let $W$ be the quasi-isomorphisms of complexes and fix a small set $S$. An $S$-graph is a family $P(s,t)$ of complexes; its category $\mathbf G_S=\prod_{(s,t)\in S^2}\mathbf V$ has the objectwise projective model structure. Let $\mathbf C_S$ be strict dg categories with object set $S$, associative unital chain-map composition $A(t,u)\otimes A(s,t)\to A(s,u)$, and functors equal to the identity on $S$. Put $\mathrm{FF}_S=\{f\mid f(s,t)\text{ is a quasi-isomorphism for every }s,t\}$. The forgetful functor $U:\mathbf C_S\to\mathbf G_S$ has a left adjoint $F$, the free dg category. Its mapping complex is
$$UF(P)(s,t)=\bigoplus_{n\geq0}\ \bigoplus_{s=x_0,\ldots,x_n=t}P(x_{n-1},x_n)\otimes\cdots\otimes P(x_0,x_1).$$
For $n=0$ the summand is $\mathbf Z[0]$ if $s=t$ and is absent otherwise. Composition concatenates paths; the unit of $F\dashv U$ inserts length-one paths.

There is a combinatorial model structure on $\mathbf C_S$ with weak equivalences $\mathrm{FF}_S$ and fibrations the mappingwise degreewise surjections. Here a model structure has retract-closed weak equivalences satisfying two-out-of-three and two weak factorization systems (cofibrations, trivial fibrations) and (trivial cofibrations, fibrations), with functorial factorizations; trivial means also a weak equivalence, and cofibrant means that the map from the initial object is a cofibration. All objects are fibrant, $F\dashv U$ is Quillen (the left adjoint preserves cofibrations and trivial cofibrations), and a cofibrant object has cofibrant mapping complexes. There is a functorial cofibrant replacement $Q_SA\to A$ that is a trivial fibration and fixes $S$.

Writing $\mathcal D=\mathbf V[W^{-1}]_\infty$, objectwise localization identifies $\mathbf G_S[W_S^{-1}]_\infty$ with $\mathcal D^{S^2}$, where $W_S$ denotes the objectwise quasi-isomorphisms. With homotopy-coherent localization as defined in [lem-coef-combinatorial-localization-presentability], on these localizations the forgetful functor $U_\infty:\mathbf C_S[\mathrm{FF}_S^{-1}]_\infty\to\mathcal D^{S^2}$ is conservative (reflects equivalences), has a left adjoint $F_\infty$, and preserves geometric realizations and, more generally, colimits indexed by $N(I)$ for every small ordinary category $I$ whose nerve is sifted. A geometric realization is a colimit indexed by $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$; sifted means that colimits of spaces indexed by that shape commute with finite products. The left adjoint is computed by $F$ applied to an objectwise cofibrant graph. Its unit is insertion of length-one paths, and its underlying graph is the displayed direct sum with derived tensors and coproducts. These adjunction identifications are coherent, including the specified unit.

source.place: Haugseng Corollaries 3.14-3.15, Lemmas 3.19-3.20 and proof of Proposition 5.2(a),(c),(e),(f); structural inputs for the fixed-object comparison in ancestor proof paragraph 2. Online source read; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this homotopy-coherent theorem. The strict dg composition uses reverse tensor order; the source uses forward order, identified here by the Koszul symmetry of complexes. The sifted-colimit assertion is restricted to nerve-indexed shapes exactly as in Lemma 3.20; it includes geometric realizations.

proof.text: Construct $F(P)$ by the displayed path sum, with the direct-sum tensor differential of [lem-coef-projective-chains-monoidal-model]. Concatenating the second path to the first places its tensor factors on the left; thus no interchange of factors is needed in the reverse-order convention. Associativity and the two identity equations reduce on each summand to the tensor associator and unit equations. Given $u:P\to UA$, define $F(P)\to A$ on a path by the tensor of its $u$-components followed by the iterated composition of $A$, and on an empty path by $\mathbf Z[0]\to A(s,s)$. Associativity makes this a dg functor, and every dg functor extending $u$ must have these components. This proves the natural adjunction and the length-one unit, including $n=0$ and $n=1$.

source.place: Lemma 3.20 (matrix monoids) and Proposition 5.2(f); direct verification of the strict universal property

proof.text:
The model axioms on $\mathbf G_S$ hold coordinatewise: take both functorial factorizations coordinatewise, and solve every lifting problem coordinatewise. A generating set consists of the generating maps in [lem-coef-projective-cochain-monoidal-model] placed in one coordinate and zero elsewhere. These single-coordinate embeddings are left adjoint to evaluation, so the lifting characterizations follow by adjunction. Apply [lem-coef-ordinary-presheaf-local-presentability] with $A=\mathbf V$ and $C$ the discrete category on $S^2$. Its hypotheses hold since $\mathbf V$ is locally presentable and complete by [lem-coef-projective-cochain-monoidal-model]. An ordinary functor from this discrete category is just its family of values, and a natural transformation is just its family of components; thus this is exactly the graph category and gives its local presentability. Left properness and tractability are coordinatewise by [lem-coef-projective-chains-monoidal-model]. Define
$$(P\star Q)(s,t)=\bigoplus_{u\in S}P(u,t)\otimes Q(s,u),\qquad E(s,t)=\begin{cases}\mathbf Z[0]&s=t,\\0&s\ne t.\end{cases}$$
Reindexing the two sums and applying the tensor associator gives the matrix associator; the diagonal summands give the unit constraints. Both partial tensor functors are left adjoints. Explicitly their right adjoints have entries
$$R_P(H)(s,u)=\prod_t\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(P(u,t),H(s,t)),\qquad L_Q(H)(u,t)=\prod_s\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(Q(s,u),H(s,t)).$$
Tensor-Hom adjunction, applied to each summand, verifies these formulas; in $L_Q$ use the symmetry of complexes. The component of the matrix pushout product $i\square_\star j$ is $\bigoplus_u i(u,t)\square_\otimes j(s,u)$. The projective pushout-product axiom makes each summand a cofibration, trivial if either matrix map is trivial. Coproducts preserve these lifting classes because fillers are chosen independently on summands. The diagonal unit $E$ is cofibrant. These checks establish the biclosed monoidal model hypotheses; $\star$ need not be symmetric.

source.place: Lemma 3.20 proof; Muro Section 10, Remark 10.2, with the matrix adjoints and pushout products written explicitly

proof.text: Verify the nonsymmetric monoid axiom for $\star$ with arbitrary auxiliary graphs, as in [lem-coef-associative-algebra-model-transfer]. Distributing an iterated matrix pushout product over its path summands gives finite tensor pushout products of component trivial cofibrations and maps $0\to C_i$, with at least one trivial cofibration. The symmetry of complexes moves the maps $0\to C_i$ to one side, identifying each such summand with $k\otimes C$, where $k$ is the iterated pushout product of the trivial cofibrations and $C$ is the tensor product of the auxiliary complexes (or the unit if none). The pushout-product axiom makes $k$ a trivial cofibration. The monoid axiom in [lem-coef-projective-chains-monoidal-model] therefore makes every component of a pushout or transfinite composite of these sums a quasi-isomorphism: a coproduct attachment is a transfinite sequence of the individual attachments, and graph colimits are coordinatewise. Retracts preserve weak equivalences by the model axioms. This checks the required nonsymmetric axiom without imposing cofibrancy on $C_i$.

source.place: Muro Definition 9.1 and Proposition 10.3, pp. 1591, 1596-1597; repairs the cofibrancy restriction printed in Haugseng Definition 3.11

proof.text: An algebra $A\star A\to A$, $E\to A$ is exactly a family of compositions $A(u,t)\otimes A(s,u)\to A(s,t)$ and identity maps, with the dg associativity and unit equations; its algebra maps are exactly dg functors fixing $S$. Under this identification the free algebra is the $F$ of Step 1. Apply [lem-coef-associative-algebra-model-transfer] to the matrix category verified in Steps 2-3. It gives the combinatorial transferred structure, the Quillen adjunction and cofibrancy of the underlying graph of a cofibrant dg category. Weak equivalences and fibrations are the asserted coordinate classes. The terminal dg category has zero mapping complexes; every $A\to0$ is mappingwise surjective, so every object is fibrant. Factor the map from the initial dg category $E\to A$ functorially as a cofibration followed by a trivial fibration $Q_SA\to A$. Every object and morphism here lies in the fixed-$S$ category, so this replacement fixes $S$.

source.place: Corollaries 3.14-3.15 and Lemma 3.20, plus the explicit model-factorization argument

proof.text: For any small discrete set $J$, the comparison $\mathbf V^J[W_J^{-1}]_\infty\to\mathcal D^J$ induced by evaluations is an equivalence. Indeed choose cofibrant representatives $X_j$ and fibrant representatives $Y_j$ and a cosimplicial frame $X_j^\bullet$ in each coordinate, using [lem-coef-cosimplicial-frame-mapping]. The objectwise frame is a frame in the product model structure because its latching colimits and weak equivalences are coordinatewise. Its mapping simplicial set is exactly $\prod_j\operatorname{Hom}(X_j^\bullet,Y_j)$, hence represents the product of the component mapping spaces (products of Kan complexes have fillers coordinatewise). This proves full faithfulness of the evaluation comparison; choosing representatives coordinatewise proves essential surjectivity. Apply this with $J=S^2$, including $J=\varnothing$.

source.place: Objectwise localization assertion in Proposition 5.2; product mapping spaces verified by the existing frame theorem

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction] to the Quillen adjunction of Step 4. Since $U$ preserves all weak equivalences, its right derived functor agrees with direct localization, and the left derived functor is $qF(P^c)$ for an objectwise cofibrant replacement $p:P^c\to P$. Step 5 identifies the graph localization with $\mathcal D^{S^2}$. The cited theorem gives the mapping-space adjunction and its coherent unit and counit, not merely a homotopy-category adjunction. In particular the unit at $qP$ is the composite of $(qp)^{-1}:qP\simeq qP^c$ with the image of the strict length-one insertion $P^c\to UF(P^c)$. The localization is presentable by [lem-coef-combinatorial-localization-presentability], applied to the combinatorial structure in Step 4.

source.place: Proposition 5.2(a),(c); derived adjunction and unit use the cited generic mapping-space theorem

proof.text: Every tensor factor in $UF(P^c)$ is cofibrant. By [lem-coef-projective-chains-monoidal-model], localizing its finite tensor products therefore computes the derived tensor products. For any discrete indexing set $J$, the ordinary coproduct $\mathbf V^J\to\mathbf V$ is left Quillen: its right adjoint is the diagonal, which preserves fibrations and trivial fibrations coordinatewise. Applying [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction] and Step 5 to this adjunction shows that a coproduct of cofibrant complexes computes their infinity-categorical coproduct. The path-sum formula of Step 1 thus gives exactly the stated underlying graph of $F_\infty$, with derived tensors and coproducts. These comparisons are natural in the graph, and the derived unit is the length-one inclusion by Step 6. The source's forward-order formula is identified with ours on homogeneous factors by reversing them with sign $(-1)^{\sum_{i<j}|a_i||a_j|}$; this is the Koszul symmetry, whose associativity and unit constraints are part of the monoidal structure. No rectification comparison is used to infer these formulas.

source.place: Proposition 5.2(f); chain-model tensor computation and derived coproduct adjunction written explicitly

proof.text: To prove conservativity, let $a:qA\to qB$ have equivalent image under $U_\infty$. Replace $A$ by $Q_SA$, and note that $B$ is fibrant by Step 4. The mapping-space representation clause of [lem-coef-cosimplicial-frame-mapping] represents the resulting component by a strict map $f:Q_SA\to B$. The image of $f(s,t)$ in $\mathcal D$ is an equivalence for every pair because the image of $a$ is, and the replacement is a weak equivalence. The saturation assertion of [lem-coef-projective-chains-monoidal-model] makes each $f(s,t)$ a quasi-isomorphism. Thus $f\in\mathrm{FF}_S$, so $qf$, and hence $a$, is an equivalence. Being an equivalence is invariant under the homotopy relating $a$ to this representative.

source.place: Proposition 5.2(e); representative and saturation arguments made explicit

proof.text: The matrix model category is left proper and tractable by Step 2 and satisfies the nonsymmetric monoid axiom by Step 3. Apply [lem-coef-associative-algebra-sifted-localization] to it and identify its strict associative algebras with $\mathbf C_S$ by Step 4. It gives preservation by $U_\infty$ of every $N(I)$-indexed colimit with $N(I)$ sifted; the comparison of Step 5 identifies its target with $\mathcal D^{S^2}$. The cited statement includes $I=\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$, so it also gives geometric-realization preservation. This proves the remaining colimit clauses directly on the strict-model localization, without using the downstream fixed-object enriched rectification theorem.

source.place: Lemma 3.19 applied as in Lemma 3.20; Proposition 5.2(e), before the monadic comparison

split_report.summary: Second reading repaired the uncited transfer and the unsupported strict-to-coherent use of categorical-algebra colimits. Nine explicit proof steps construct the path adjunction, verify the matrix model and strong monoid axiom, apply two generic associative-algebra inputs, and prove product localization, coherent derived units, the derived path formula and conservativity with existing model-category nodes. Two new statement-only inputs and one exact Mathlib leaf for ordinary presheaf local presentability; no statement change.
split_report.blueprint: Realizes the fixed-object strict dg free/forgetful structural input used before passage to coherent coefficient diagrams in the ancestor proof paragraph 2.

I checked the item's statement against Haugseng arXiv:1312.3881v4 Lemma 3.20 (with Cor. 3.14/3.15, Def. 3.18 and Lemma 3.19), read online in the HTML version. The source error is confirmed: printed Def. 3.11 takes only cofibrant X_i, while the proof of Cor. 3.14 needs arbitrary objects. The new nodes use Muro's arbitrary-object axiom, a stronger and correct hypothesis, and Step 3 verifies it for the matrix product from the chain node's monoid axiom (arbitrary C). Step checks: I recomputed both matrix right adjoints R_P and L_Q, and the pushout-product component ⊕_u i(u,t)□j(s,u). The reverse-order path concatenation needs no signs. Algebras for the matrix product are exactly dg categories with object set S and the unit E is initial. In Step 5 the evaluations are left Quillen (right adjoint puts X at one coordinate, 0 elsewhere), so the frame node identifies the comparison maps. Coproduct ⊣ diagonal computes derived coproducts. Conservativity goes through a strict representative Q_S A→B and saturation. Every hypothesis of the sifted lemma is checked in Steps 2-4. Small cases: S empty, a single object (tensor algebra), the zero graph (F(0)=E), the zero dg category as terminal object, and Z/2 as a non-cofibrant complex. The Mathlib leaf is verified at Presheaf.lean:90-95. All cited nodes are in unit sk-prop-sf-biduality-general, there are no tool_uses, no cycle and no SGA. The DAG and blueprint searches found no duplicate.
